PullRequest.Title: Agent Host: declare and turn-correlate forwarded compaction telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Problem For Copilot Chat we have `summarizedConversationHistory`, plus `response.success` with `requestKind: conversation-compaction` for the summarization call. Agent Host (Copilot CLI provider) has no usable equivalent: - The runtime already sends `session_compaction_start` and `session_compaction_complete`, which `CopilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder` re-emits as `copilotSdk/session_compaction_*`. Neither had a `__GDPR__` declaration. - These events can't be joined to the Agent Host turn. The forwarder only stamps the host `turnId` on `response.*` events. - The runtime never emitted `response.success` for compaction calls. That's fixed in github/copilot-agent-runtime#28328. Once those rows arrive, the existing response path would wait 100ms for a model-call→turn mapping that never comes for summarization calls (they never complete a turn's model call), and would then drop the turn. ## Changes ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph RT["Copilot runtime"] C["Compaction attempt
compactionAttemptId"] --> SE["Session events
session.compaction_start / _complete"] C --> TB["Telemetry rows
session_compaction_start / _complete
response.success / .error
requestKind = conversation-compaction"] end subgraph AH["Agent Host"] CAS["CopilotAgentSession
_recordCompactionTurn"] -- "record(attemptId, owning root turn)" --> CTC[("CompactionTurnCorrelation
attemptId → host turn or none")] R{"CopilotAgent
_forwardGitHubTelemetry"} R -- "session_compaction_*" --> FC["_forwardCompactionTelemetry"] R -- "response.* (compaction)" --> FR["_forwardResponseTelemetry"] R -. "other response.*" .-> MC["model-call correlation (unchanged)"] FC -- "resolve(compaction_attempt_id)" --> CTC FR -- "resolve(compaction_attempt_id)" --> CTC FC --> F["CopilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder"] FR --> F end SE -- "SDK session events
(ordered with turn start/end)" --> CAS TB -- "onGitHubTelemetry
(separate channel)" --> R F --> OUT["copilotSdk/session_compaction_*
copilotSdk/response.*
turnId = owning host turn
+ correlation outcome"] ``` - **GDPR.** Declare `copilotSdk/session_compaction_start` and `copilotSdk/session_compaction_complete` with every field the runtime builders emit (including the `summarizer_*` progress and attempt metrics), a `CopilotCompactionTurnCorrelation` fragment, and `compaction_attempt_id` on `copilotSdk/response.*`. - **Record the owner from session events.** `CopilotAgentSession` records the owning root turn for each `compactionAttemptId` when it sees `session.compaction_start` (or `session.compaction_complete` if start was missed). Session events arrive in order with turn start and end, so this is the turn that started the compaction. - **Look the owner up for every compaction row.** `CopilotAgent` resolves `compaction_attempt_id` for `session_compaction_*` rows and for `response.*` rows with `requestKind = conversation-compaction`. It replaces the runtime `turnId` with the owning host turn, or removes it, and adds the correlation outcome: `mappingAvailable`, `mappingWaited`, `waitExpired`, `noOwningTurn`, `missingAttemptId` or `sessionNotFound`. Compaction responses no longer wait for a model-call mapping that never arrives. ### Why not use the active turn? Telemetry rows arrive on a separate channel from session events, and a background compaction can outlive the turn that started it. Stamping whichever turn is active when a row arrives would attribute the summarizer's response and completion to the next turn. Keying by attempt keeps all rows of one compaction on the turn that started it: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant RT as Runtime participant S as CopilotAgentSession participant C as CompactionTurnCorrelation participant A as CopilotAgent Note over S: Turn A active RT->>S: session.compaction_start (attempt X) S->>C: record(X, A) RT->>A: session_compaction_start (X) A->>C: resolve(X) C-->>A: A Note over S: Turn A ends, user starts turn B RT->>A: response.success (conversation-compaction, X) A->>C: resolve(X) C-->>A: A, not the active turn B RT->>A: session_compaction_complete (X) A->>C: resolve(X) C-->>A: A Note over C,A: An early row waits up to 100 ms for record() ``` ## Product impact No user-facing change. Compaction telemetry from Agent Host can now be joined to `agentHost.turnCompleted` by `turnId`. This PR doesn't depend on github/copilot-agent-runtime#28328: the start/complete rows and compaction `response.error` rows already carry `compaction_attempt_id` today, and compaction `response.success` rows are handled once that runtime change ships. ## How to test `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/compactionTurnCorrelation.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder.test.ts`

Scenarios.Scenario: A compaction starts or completes while an Agent Host turn is active, and the runtime emits session_compaction_start/session_compaction_complete telemetry.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK session-event handler synchronously performs O(1) owner lookup and one bounded LRU record before returning; the separate GitHub telemetry callback resolves the mapping and publishes telemetry. Compaction/model execution and the user turn do not await the GitHub telemetry callback, which is launched with void, so correlation and publication are off the user critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive an existing telemetry notification from the Copilot runtime connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two session-compaction rows per attempt under normal operation, plus any separately emitted response row; no collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runtime telemetry callback received each row and routed it directly to the generic forwarder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already received before the changed correlation path runs; callback processing is detached from turn progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build, sanitize, and publish one scalar telemetry object through ITelemetryService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one publication for each runtime session-compaction telemetry row; the diff does not duplicate or add publications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The generic forward path already built and published one telemetry object for each row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the user critical path; synchronous work is bounded by the telemetry row's scalar property count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of compaction attempts and their two telemetry rows; there is no dependence on conversation message/token count because only bounded scalar metrics and identifiers are copied.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SDK session events are ordered. Telemetry callbacks are detached and may overlap, but waiters coalesce on one DeferredPromise per attempt; each row has its own bounded timer and there is no expensive remote operation under that concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The start session event warms the attempt-to-turn LRU. A warm telemetry row resolves immediately; a cold row shares a per-attempt pending entry and waits at most 100 ms. The owner cache is capped at 200 attempts per session, and completion refreshes the same key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed handlers, bounded LRU, 100 ms timeout, detached callback, and unchanged single publication are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact compaction frequency varies with session length and context limits, but realistic cardinality is a few rows per compaction rather than per message/token.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded O(1) map/timer work and does not increase expensive-boundary call count or place it on turn progress.

Scenarios.Scenario: A compaction telemetry row arrives before the ordered session event records its owning turn.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The detached telemetry task allocates/reuses one pending entry and awaits up to 100 ms; record() completes all same-attempt waiters when the session event arrives. Nothing in chat rendering, input, compaction execution, or turn completion awaits this task.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the telemetry row after correlation resolves or expires.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One publication per inbound row, unchanged from before the diff; waiting changes timing only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The row was published immediately by the generic path; response rows could already wait up to 100 ms on model-call correlation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delayed only on the telemetry path by at most 100 ms and detached from product progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct out-of-order compaction attempt IDs and at most the start, completion, and response rows sharing each attempt ID.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent attempt IDs can wait concurrently without a global limiter, but each contributes only a DeferredPromise, counters, and short timer(s); natural cardinality is bounded by concurrently emitted compaction rows across live sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A miss creates one pending DeferredPromise per attempt. Multiple rows share it; after every waiter expires the map entry is removed, and successful recording moves the result into a 200-entry LRU. Missing IDs do not allocate pending entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: resolve(), waiter accounting, raceTimeout timer cancellation, and map deletion are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The relative ordering rate between SDK session events and telemetry notifications is not quantified, but each miss is time-bounded and resource-light.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Waiting is bounded, coalesced per attempt, cleaned after expiry, and off the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: A conversation-compaction response.success/response.error row is forwarded after its summarization model call.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The response path now resolves by compaction attempt. Warm mappings forward immediately; a cold mapping waits at most 100 ms. The runtime callback is detached, so the wait does not block the turn or compaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sanitize and publish one response telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One publication per runtime response row, both before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing response path attempted model-call correlation and could wait the same 100 ms before publishing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off product progress; only telemetry delivery timing changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One response row per compaction summarizer request emitted by the runtime; no per-history-item processing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rows for independent attempts resolve independently; there is no serialization or expensive-operation burst added by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the same capped attempt LRU and per-attempt pending coalescing. A recorded attempt avoids the former model-call correlation miss; an unrecorded attempt retains the same 100 ms upper-bound behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the before/after branches both have a maximum 100 ms correlation wait and the callback ownership is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future runtime versions may emit successful compaction response rows more often, but count remains tied to compaction model calls and publication count is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This changes the correlation key and usually removes an unproductive wait; it does not add boundary calls or block user work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A long-lived session accumulates many completed compaction attempts and is later disposed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each start/complete event records one key in a per-session LRU; session disposal removes the owning session object from the live-session map. Outstanding detached resolutions retain it for at most their 100 ms timeout.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Lifetime number of compaction attempts in one session; effective retained cardinality is capped at 200 owner entries plus currently waiting attempt IDs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pending attempts can overlap, but each waiter has a bounded timeout and each per-attempt entry is removed after its final waiter; no cleanup boundary is serialized with user work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: LRU eviction bounds completed mappings to 200. Pending entries are removed when recorded or when the last waiter expires. No negative result is pinned indefinitely.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cache and pending-entry lifecycle from the implementation; moderate for runtime-level compaction concurrency, which does not affect the bounded per-entry mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum number of simultaneous compactions permitted by the runtime was not established, but retained completed state is hard-capped and pending state lifetime is 100 ms.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable memory regression. Completed state is capped, pending state has explicit removal, and disposal makes the session collectible after short detached waits settle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced compaction session events, out-of-order correlation, response forwarding, telemetry serialization/publication, cache eviction, pending-wait cleanup, session disposal, and callback concurrency. The PR adds only bounded O(1) correlation work, preserves one telemetry publication per inbound row, and keeps waits off the user critical path; no high-confidence performance finding or regression-fix learning signal was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
